title: Ambient Dataloops: Generative Models for Dataset Refinement
claim: Repeatedly using a model to restore its own training data progressively improves both dataset quality and model samples.
layout: 3 image rows with downward arrows, model sample grids at right, diagonal arrows
description: Three horizontal rows of six generated images each, labeled D0, D1 and D2 on the left. D0 images (wolf, owls, rabbit cartoon, Groot, dinosaur head, farmhouse) show artifacts and blur. D1 and D2 show the same prompts, each cleaner and sharper. Short downward arrows join the rows, and a long vertical arrow on the far left is labeled 'Dataset Refinement'. At the right are two 2x2 grids of samples (boots, steaming cup, jellyfish diver, panda with potions) labeled M1 and M2. Diagonal black arrows go from D0 to M1, from M1 to D1, from D1 to M2, and from M2 to D2. A vertical arrow on the far right is labeled 'Model Refinement'. The eye goes first to the colorful image rows, then follows the arrows.
caption: Dataset and model evolution across loops of our method. $D_0$ shows synthetically generated images from DiffusionDB [ref], a dataset used for text-to-image generative modeling. These images have artifacts due to learning errors of the underlying model. We train a model on this dataset, $M_1$, that we use to improve its own training set, leading to a "restored" dataset $D_1$. Successive iterations of this process lead to a co-evolution of both the model and the dataset -- see dataset $D_2$ and model $M_1$ respectively. We avoid catastrophic self-consuming loops by accounting for learning errors at each iteration using Ambient Diffusion [ref] techniques for learning from imperfect data.
abstract: We propose Ambient Dataloops, an iterative framework for refining datasets that makes it easier for diffusion models to learn the underlying data distribution. Modern datasets contain samples of highly varying quality, and training directly on such heterogeneous data often yields suboptimal models. We propose a dataset-model co-evolution process; at each iteration of our method, the dataset becomes progressively higher quality, and the model improves accordingly. To avoid destructive self-consuming loops, at each generation, we treat the synthetically improved samples as noisy, but at a slightly lower noisy level than the previous iteration, and we use Ambient Diffusion techniques for learning under corruption. Empirically, Ambient Dataloops achieve state-of-the-art performance in unconditional and text-conditional image generation and de novo protein design. We further provide a theoretical justification for the proposed framework that captures the benefits of the data looping procedure.
